transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-08-18 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Marisol (Redwood SE), Evan (CSM), Aisha (CISO, Veridian), Tom (Eng Lead), Priya (PM), Luca (DevOps)

Summary (auto): Quick sync on SSO + audit logs, clarify retention on logs vs model telemetry, set action items to get Okta test tenant connected and verify Splunk forwarding.

[00:00] Samir: Okay hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, quick roll call? I'll start, Samir here from Redwood. Marisol, Evan?
[00:07] Marisol: Marisol here, hello.
[00:09] Evan: Evan on the line.
[00:11] Aisha: Aisha, CISO at Veridian.
[00:13] Tom: Tom, engineering.
[00:15] Priya: Priya, product.
[00:16] Luca: Luca, DevOps.
[00:18] Samir: Great. High level — this is our weekly POC check-in, wanted to focus today on the security bits: SSO onboarding, audit logs, and retention. I sent an agenda but we'll keep it loose.

[02:02] Priya: Quick context from our side — we're doing a 6-week pilot, right? Primary blockers are that we need SSO in production-like way, and audit trails must be exportable to our SIEM for SOC2 evidence. Also retention rules, like 90 days for logs and 365 for some artifacts.

[02:25] Aisha: Yes, and to be clear we need immutable audit logs for any access to PII and we need proof of deletion when something is removed. That's a legal ask.

[03:10] Samir: Totally. On Redwood side, we have three deployment modes we discussed: Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Redwood Private. For the pilot you ran on Hosted, but for compliance you might want Redwood Private or Dedicated with VPC peering. Marisol, can you walk through SSO options?

[03:35] Marisol: Sure. We support SAML 2.0 for single sign-on, SCIM for provisioning/ de-provisioning, and RBAC via groups. In the Private flow we can integrate directly with your IdP over SAML and enable SCIM for user sync. A small caveat — the initial tokenizer, uh, the initial admin needs manual setup to bootstrap the SCIM mapping. There was a typo in our doc where "SCIM" was transcribed as "skim" — ignore that.

[04:10] Tom: For SAML we use Okta. We can provide a sandbox tenant. For SCIM, we need to sync groups automatically, that was one of our must-haves.

[04:22] Marisol: Okta is our most common IdP — we have step-by-step. We also support metadata file upload or a metadata URL. We can also demo group mapping, and group-to-role mapping, e.g., devs -> infer-dev, security -> view-only.

[04:50] Luca: Small ops question — what's the auth flow for API keys? Do they still exist after SCIM? We want machine-to-machine tokens scoped to service accounts.

[05:02] Samir: Good question. Yes — SCIM and SSO are about human users. For service accounts we support long-lived API keys scoped to roles; in Private deployments you can rotate them via your KMS. We can also enable HSM-backed keys if you require.

[05:35] Aisha: Can you talk about audit logs — format, retention, and whether they contain payloads? We can’t have raw PII in logs.

[05:48] Marisol: Right. Audit logs capture authentication events, model request metadata (time, model id, token counts), and operational events like scaling. By default request payloads are not included in the audit trail; payload logging is opt-in and can be redacted. We have a redaction pipeline that can strip or hash PII prior to writing logs. For the pilot we recommend sending structured logs to your Splunk instance via syslog or HTTP event collector.

[06:20] Tom: Is there an option for full fidelity logs to be stored only within the customer's VPC? We want to avoid any persisted payloads outside our control.

[06:35] Marisol: In Redwood Private yes — logs can be routed to a customer-owned logging endpoint and we can disable retention on our control plane for payload content. For Hosted we can also enable dedicated retention windows and partial redaction but full isolation requires Private/Dedicated.

[07:05] Priya: For the pilot success criterion, we said: 1) SSO + SCIM functional in staging; 2) audit export works to Splunk; 3) retention policies enforced and documented. Is that still accurate?

[07:18] Evan: That's right — and also low false positives in our quality checks, but that's outside security.

[08:00] Aisha: I've reviewed the security packet you shared last week, there were a few items missing — e.g., the last SOC2 attestation date and the encryption-at-rest details for the KV cache. Can you confirm?

[08:13] Samir: Yes, apologies. I will attach the SOC2 Type II report — the latest is from Q1 2027 — and a note on encryption for the KV cache. Our default disk-level encryption is AES-256 and in Private we can bring your own keys via KMS/HSM. I'll add those to the packet.

[08:40] Aisha: Good. Also need to understand retention behavior for KV cache — we use prefix caching for assistant sessions and we need to know how long keys live and how to evict partial prefixes.

[09:02] Marisol: The KV cache TTL is configurable per deployment; in Hosted we suggested 7 days for pilot but we can configure 0 to disable caching, or longer up to 30 days. In Private you control both TTL and explicit deletion. Note: eviction is by prefix and by LRU heuristics at high capacity. I'll send a snippet in the follow-up showing the config YAML.

[10:00] Tom: About evidence for audits — can you produce logs that show read/write to sensitive datasets, and show the actor (user/service) and the request id?

[10:17] Marisol: Yes, each event includes actor, request_id, timestamp, and resource path. If you need it formatted to your audit schema we can transform to JSON lines and add fields as needed. For Splunk we usually forward JSON lines.

[11:10] Luca: We use Splunk HTTP event collector (HEC). Any sample config?

[11:18] Marisol: Yep, I'll share a HEC sample and a Terraform snippet to spin up the forwarder. For the Private demo I can show forwarding directly to your HEC endpoint in the staging environment.

[12:04] Priya: One tricky bit: eDiscovery and deletion. Legal will want a record proving deletion occurred and when. Do you emit deletion events?

[12:16] Marisol: We emit a deletion event with metadata including actor, deletion request id, affected prefixes, and TTL. The deletion event is immutable in the audit trail — it's an append-only entry. Full payload deletion from storage can be triggered and we can provide the hash of the deleted object as proof. There's also a documented retention purge job schedule we can reference.

[13:00] Aisha: On SOC2 — can you confirm scope? Does it include Redwood Private? We need to know if the SOC2 covers the control plane and the parts we run in our VPC.

[13:15] Samir: Good question. Our SOC2 Type II currently covers the Redwood control plane and hosted services. For Private, the control plane components we manage are in scope, but customer-managed infrastructure (your VPC resources) are your scope. We'll annotate responsibilities in the shared SOC2 matrix.

[13:50] Aisha: Okay we need that matrix spelled out.

[14:05] Samir: I'll include a RACI-style matrix in the packet — who manages what and which evidence we can provide.

[15:00] Tom: Regarding network controls — do you support VPC peering and private endpoints? Latency matters but security trumps for us.

[15:12] Marisol: Yes VPC peering and private links are supported for Dedicated and Private. In pilot we can set up a private endpoint to your VPC in the staging region.

[16:00] Luca: About metrics we log — do you capture token counts and model IDs for billing? We need that for cost reconciliation but want to ensure no prompt leakage.

[16:15] Marisol: We log token counts and model_id, but not prompt content unless explicitly enabled. For billing we include a hashed prompt id so you can reconcile without seeing the content.

[17:20] Priya: Are there known limitations with SAML group sync and nested groups? We use nested groups in Okta heavily.

[17:33] Marisol: Current SCIM mapping doesn't expand nested groups automatically; it's a one-level map. We can implement a custom mapping during POC, but out-of-the-box it's one level. That was a gap we noted in the integration doc.

[18:05] Aisha: That could impact our RBAC — if nested groups don't map we might lose role inheritance.

[18:14] Marisol: Agreed. For the pilot we'll do a quick script to flatten your group structure; it's a common workaround and we'll provide it.

[19:00] Samir: Let's cover audit-forwarding specifics — Marisol can demo a sample event and show how it's parsed in Splunk, right?

[19:12] Marisol: Yes. Example event — timestamp, actor, request_id, model_id, token_count, status, and an optional redacted payload pointer. We can also tag events with env:pilot and customer:veridian for filtering.

[20:00] Luca: Any PII leakage risk from model-generated outputs in logs? We need to be sure generated text isn't stored unless we approve.

[20:12] Marisol: Right — by default we do not log model outputs. You have to enable debug or payload logging. If enabled, you can configure a pre-log redaction step or route payloads to your private S3 with server-side encryption and lifecycle rules.

[21:00] Aisha: For the SOC2 demo, we'll want to see evidence of user provisioning workflows, and a sample of audit logs showing a user creation and de-provision. Is that feasible in the staging run?

[21:15] Marisol: Absolutely — we'll create a user in Okta, SCIM will provision, you'll see a create event in the audit log and then we'll de-provision and show the deletion event.

[22:30] Tom: Let's talk SLA expectations for pilot — we know prod SLAs aren't in place, but we want to set an internal SLO for latency and error rate for this workload. Any suggestions?

[22:45] Samir: For the pilot, let's aim for P99 latency under 500ms for short completions on the dedicated path; but that depends on model choice and batch settings. We'll propose a baseline runbook and we'll instrument token-level latencies in the dashboard.

[23:40] Priya: On the dashboard — can we get a per-route auditor view? Security wants a route-level change history.

[23:50] Marisol: You can — the Console includes route history and token-level cost/latency. We also expose audit events for route changes.

[24:30] Aisha: A few more clarifications: backup retention for logs (is this separate from primary retention?), and the ability to freeze data for legal hold.

[24:45] Marisol: Backups are a separate retention scope; we can retain immutable backup snapshots for a longer period if needed. For legal hold we have a freeze flag that prevents deletion during purge cycles. We will document the process for triggering a legal hold.

[25:30] Luca: Can Redwood generate a signed proof-of-deletion? We need a signed artifact to prove deletion to auditors.

[25:42] Samir: Yes, we can generate a signed deletion manifest including hashes and timestamps. For Private deployments we can sign with your KMS keys if you prefer.

[26:30] Priya: Are there any extra costs for audit-forwarding or extended retention? We need to budget for storage and egress.

[26:45] Samir: There is generally a small forwarding cost and storage charge for long-term retention. For pilot we can absorb some costs but we'll include estimates in the pricing note.

[27:30] Aisha: Will you provide a retention configuration example that distinguishes logs, metrics, and payloads? We want a matrix.

[27:40] Marisol: Yes — I'll attach a retention matrix: log types, default retention, options, and whether we support purge or legal hold.

[28:20] Tom: About the KV cache again — if we disable caching in pilot, will it have a performance hit? Curious how big.

[28:33] Marisol: Expect a 10-30% token cost increase and potential latency uptick for repeated prefixes. We'll run a quick bench to quantify for your workload.

[29:10] Priya: Could you run that bench for a subset of our prompt templates?

[29:20] Marisol: Yes — please share sample prompt templates or a small prompt corpus and we'll run the bench on Dedicated and Hosted configs.

[29:45] Samir: I'll follow up with an email to capture the corpus and confirm the bench parameters.

[30:30] Aisha: Anything else on compliance? We're mostly comfortable as long as we get SOC2, the RACI matrix, and log forwarding working. Also fine-grained RBAC and proof-of-deletion.

[30:45] Samir: Noted. On missing items: Marisol will demo SCIM group flattening script, provide Splunk HEC snippet, and SE will stand up staging with forwarding enabled.

[31:20] Marisol: I'll also include the YAML of the retention TTL and an example of disabling KV cache.

[32:05] Luca: Quick note — our security team will want a short 20-minute follow-up once SCIM is set up to validate group mappings.

[32:15] Aisha: Yes, schedule after SCIM test.

[33:00] Evan: I'll coordinate timeline — sounds like we want SCIM test by next week.

[33:10] Samir: Proposed milestones: 1) Samir sends SOC2 + RACI by 2027-08-20, 2) Luca provides Okta sandbox by 2027-08-22, 3) Marisol stands up staging with Splunk HEC by 2027-08-25, 4) SCIM validation call w/ security by 2027-08-26.

[34:00] Priya: Works for us. Also please include the TTL config and the bench plan in the follow-up.

[34:15] Marisol: Will do. Any blockers?

[34:25] Aisha: None immediate, just timelines. We might ask for a tighter retention (30 days) for some dev logs but we'll surface specifics.

[35:00] Tom: One more nit — does Redwood have a vulnerability disclosure program and are CVEs tracked? We need to know how quickly critical issues are patched.

[35:12] Samir: Yes we have a vuln disclosure program and patch SLAs documented. I'll include the program link and our typical patch windows.

[36:00] Priya: On billing reconciliation — we'll need token-level reports that match our usage numbers for cost center tagging. Is that available?

[36:10] Marisol: Yes per-request metadata includes cost centers (you can pass a tag) and we can provide a CSV export or S3 delivery of usage reports.

[37:00] Luca: Are there any constraints around region residency? We require EU residency for some datasets.

[37:12] Marisol: We support regional deployments. For EU-resident data we can pin your pilot to the EU region and ensure logs and model telemetry remain in-region when using Dedicated or Private. Hosted may have cross-region copies for failover; we'll document residency guarantees.

[37:50] Aisha: Make sure that gets called out in the RACI and SOC2 matrix.

[38:20] Samir: Will do. Any final questions?

[38:50] Priya: Nothing more. Appreciate the clarity.

[39:10] Tom: Quick demo ask: can Marisol show an example Splunk search to surface deletion events?

[39:18] Marisol: Yes — example: index=redwood_events customer=veridian event_type=deletion | table _time actor request_id resource_hash. I'll add that to the follow-up doc.

[40:30] Aisha: Good. Also will need a legal hold test — can we freeze a dataset and then unfreeze?

[40:41] Marisol: Yes that's supported. We'll demonstrate freeze/unfreeze and show the audit events.

[41:20] Samir: Ok let's recap the action items and owners.

[41:25] Samir: Samir will share SOC2 and security packet by Friday 2027-08-20.
[41:30] Marisol: Marisol will stand up staging and send Splunk HEC and Terraform snippets by 2027-08-25.
[41:36] Luca: Luca will provide Okta sandbox metadata by 2027-08-22.
[41:40] Priya: Priya will confirm retention windows and PII redaction policy details by 2027-08-27.

[42:10] Evan: We'll schedule the SCIM validation call for 2027-08-26.

[42:20] Aisha: Sounds good. Anything else?

[43:00] Samir: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with a single doc and meeting invite for the SCIM validation.

[43:10] Tom: Thanks.

[43:20] Priya: Thanks all.

[44:00] Meeting end
